html:
The Plantation of Ulster was the settling of the northern Irish province of Ulster with Protestant colonists from Scotland and England, organised by the crown from 1609.

Ulster had been the most Gaelic part of Ireland. After the Nine Years' War against the English crown, its leading lords fled to the continent in 1607, the Flight of the Earls. Their lands were confiscated and granted to settlers, London companies and loyal soldiers, who built new towns such as Derry, renamed Londonderry.

The native Catholic Irish were pushed onto poorer land. The settlers, many of them Scottish Presbyterians, became a large community with a separate identity. The divide between them and the Catholic Irish runs through the rising of 1641, the Boyne, and the partition of Ireland in 1921 to the Troubles.
sum: The Plantation of Ulster was the settling of the northern Irish province of Ulster with Protestant colonists from Scotland and England, organised by the crown from 1609.
